reviewed.files: IOHIDEventService.cpp 856c46ec -> 852df3bb; PDHIDEventQueue.cpp c7a2f35b -> dd2eb4e1; PDHIDEventQueue.h b2fdd461 -> ee96bc82. The before hashes equal sources/puredarwin-m1-desktop; my scratch replay reproduces all three after hashes. PDM1SPIHID.cpp is unchanged (b38f0087).

verdict: APPROVE the kernel publication patch for the isolated IOHIDFamily SDK build and the regression/native KCs. Pitfalls P1-P7 of pdhid-publication-design-review.json are addressed. F1 is an evidence-design requirement for any native-keyboard qualification that uses a KC still containing PDSerialHID; it is not a code defect.

verified.single_owner: One gPublishCall, allocated with THREAD_CALL_OPTIONS_ONCE and installed by CAS (losers freed). Only its worker touches majors, devfs node pointers and the per-kind attempt/error state. Callers only OR bits into gPublishRequests and thread_call_enter. XNU thread_call.c:714-723/760-770: entering a running ONCE call sets RESCHEDULE (immediate or with deadline), and finish (:1588-1610) re-queues it. Every run re-reads gPublishRequests, so a request arriving mid-run is never lost. Edge: if a request's immediate enter and the worker's own 1 s enter_delayed both happen in one run, the later call sets the deadline, so the request waits at most 1 s.
verified.repend_and_budget: pd_hid_request_publication returns early when every requested bit is already ready or stopped, and (once the call exists) when no new bit is added, so repeated requests neither speed up the 1 s retry nor consume its budget. A new capability wakes the owner early.
verified.bounded_retry: Per kind, kPublishAttemptLimit is 60 worker attempts, 1 s apart. Logs: one deferral on attempt 1 with an API-specific error (storage/major/devfs/node), one 'ready kind= attempts= early_drops= (endpoint, not input proof)', and one 'publication refused' when exhausted. Exhaustion sets gPublishStopped (primary and alias), which is terminal for the boot; later requests cannot restart it.
verified.no_reentry: The IOBSD notifier is gone; readiness is devfs_is_ready polling in the worker. No lock is held across cdevsw_add/devfs_make_node; a re-entering publisher can only re-pend the ONCE call. devfs_make_node uses a '%s' format.
verified.readiness_before_visibility: The worker sets up storage (CAS'd gKbdLock, gLEDLock, gConsoleCall; CAS'd gMouseLock) and sets gQueueReady (OSBitOrAtomic, full barrier) before creating the node. open/read on both nodes return ENXIO until the matching gQueueReady bit is set, and the keyboard open sets gKbdGrabbed only after that check.
verified.fast_push: PDHIDPushKeyboardEvent and pd_hid_mouse_enqueue never allocate or publish. Before ready they only increment the early-drop counter and return; after ready they use the installed lock and ring. The keyboard sequence is now assigned under gKbdLock in the same critical section as the slot write (fixes P6, matching the mouse path). The console kick uses the installed gConsoleCall.
verified.producer_binding: Publication is requested only from IOHIDEventService::start, right after _readyForInputReports = true, from the service's parsed usage pairs: GenericDesktop Keyboard/Keypad request the keyboard queue, Mouse the mouse queue. start cannot fail after this point (registerService, return true), so an endpoint always has a successfully started producer. A native SPI keyboard therefore yields a keyboard endpoint only. No report is manufactured.
verified.led_contract: The header documents that LED handlers run under the LED lock and must not re-enter Register/Unregister. The patch adds no LED handler; native SPI LED work needs a separate review.
verified.tests: test_publication.py: 23/23 OK here; verify_candidate.py: PASS (hashes, split/combined replay).

findings.text: PDSerialHID starts at boot with keyboard and mouse usage pairs, so with this patch it publishes /dev/usb_hid_kbd and /dev/usb_hid_mouse at boot, and it feeds the same shared keyboard queue as a native SPI keyboard. In the planned 50-member (replacement-only) and 51-member (plus native) KCs, which both still contain PDSerialHID, endpoint existence, the 'ready kind=1' log and even queue records cannot be attributed to the native keyboard. For native qualification either (a) use a KC without PDSerialHID, or (b) log the requesting service identity (class and registry ID) on the first request per kind, and require zero SOH/PDSerialHID bytes in the host TX ledger after the launcher command. Without that, the endpoint proves nothing about the native keyboard.

Host-origin runs change their observable ordering: the nodes now appear at boot rather than after DL10/DL11 PRIME lines. Function is unaffected: the guest stat-wait passes immediately, priming events are queued, and the compositor's open-time drain discards up to 128 rounds. Earlier receipts that cited 'published after PRIME' remain valid for their own captures; do not expect that ordering from KCs with this patch.

The 60 x 1 s budget starts at the first request. IOHIDFamily services such as PDSerialHID can start before BSD init, so devfs readiness must arrive within 60 s of that on this platform. The deferral/ready/refused logs will show it; consider adding uptime to the deferral and ready lines for direct measurement.

Nodes remain 0666 (pitfall P8). Acceptable in the single-user RAM root; a production endpoint should be 0600 or a console group. PDHIDAllocateMouseIndex is still a non-atomic increment (pre-existing; IOHIDEventService CASes only its own static).

scope: Read-only patch review, scratch replay and host tests. No source-tree changes and no hardware.
